string_literal_length_goal.hint: Each case has a remaining goal of the form `0 < "literal".length` — these are closed concrete propositions (no free variables), so use `decide` or `norm_num` to close them. Add `· decide` (or `· norm_num`) after each case branch, or add `all_goals decide` at the end to close all such goals at once. Do NOT use `omega` — it cannot evaluate un-reduced string literal lengths.

prefix_not_defeq.error:
not definitionally equal
  String.isPrefixOf a b
prefix_not_defeq.hint:
String-level prefix goals cannot be closed in this Lean version: `String.startsWith` is implemented through `String.Slice.Pattern.ForwardPattern`, and `String.isPrefixOf` does not reduce either — `simp`, `rfl`, `decide` and unfolding all fail on them.
Convert to `List Char`, where the goal is trivial:
  simp [String.toList_append, List.isPrefixOf]
This closes goals of the form `a.toList.isPrefixOf (a ++ b).toList = true`.
Better still, state the property over `List Char` in the first place — model the function as taking `List Char` rather than `String`, and `simp [List.isPrefixOf]`, `List.prefix_append` and `List.take_append` all apply directly.
Use `.toList`, NOT `.data` — `.data` does not reduce. Do NOT use `String.isPrefixOf_iff`, `String.isPrefixOf_append_left` or `List.isPrefixOf_append_left`: they do not exist. `String.toList_append` takes no explicit arguments, so pass it to `simp`, never `exact`.

String-level prefix goals cannot be closed in this Lean version: `String.startsWith` is implemented through `String.Slice.Pattern.ForwardPattern`, and `String.isPrefixOf` does not reduce either — `simp`, `rfl`, `decide` and unfolding all fail on them.

no_goals.hint:
A tactic ran but there were no goals left — an earlier tactic already closed everything. Common causes:
(1) A tactic like `simp at h`, `exact`, or `rw` closed the goal and you have extra tactics after it. Remove them.
(2) In an `iff` proof with `constructor` + `split_ifs at h`, if `simp at h` in one branch fails to close by contradiction (e.g. `h : Except.ok X = Except.error ()`), that sub-goal leaks out and the backward-direction `·` bullet ends up on the wrong goal. Fix: replace bare `simp at h` with `exact absurd h (by simp)` or `simp [Except.ok.injEq] at h` to guarantee the contradiction closes the branch.
(3) For the backward direction of `iff` with `if-then-else`: prefer
    `simp only [functionName, if_pos h]`
  over `unfold` + `rw [if_pos h]` — the `rw` closes the goal automatically via rfl, leaving nothing for subsequent tactics.

no_goals_in_cases.error:
No goals
cases branch already closed
no_goals_in_cases.hint: One of the `cases` (or `match`) branches already closed its goal before all its tactics ran. Each branch must be proved independently — remove any tactics that appear after the goal is already closed in that branch.

split_ifs_no_if.error: split_ifs requires an if-then-else but no if-then-else was found
split_ifs_no_if.hint: `split_ifs` requires a visible `if`-`then`-`else` — there is none here. Do NOT call `split_ifs`. Instead: (1) use `obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := h` to split a conjunction hypothesis, (2) then case on the list to reduce it to a singleton (`cases l with | nil => simp at h1 | cons a t => cases t with | nil => ... | cons b t => omega`), (3) then `simp` to close the membership goal.

constructor_generic.hint: The goal is not a conjunction/disjunction — `constructor` does not apply. Use `exact h`, `assumption`, `linarith`, `ring`, or `omega` to close it directly.

constructor_arithmetic.hint: The goal is an arithmetic equation — `constructor` does not apply here. In a list-induction cons case with a 'all elements satisfy P' hypothesis, the pattern is: (1) extract the head fact with `have hhead := hweights _ (by simp)` (or `List.mem_cons_self`), (2) build the tail hypothesis with `have htail : ∀ x ∈ tl, P x := fun x hx => hweights x (by simp [hx])`, (3) apply the IH to the tail, (4) close with `simp [hhead, mul_zero, ih]` or `linarith`/`ring`.

simp_no_progress.hint: simp cannot simplify the target. Common causes and fixes: (1) Branch order after `split_ifs` depends on the guard shape: for `if !boolField then none else body`, the FIRST branch has `hGuard: !boolField = true` (meaning bool is FALSE, function returns none) — `simp at h` closes `h: none = some _` THERE, and the SECOND branch is the real-content branch. For a plain `if cond then body else none`, it is the opposite: first branch is real content. Check which branch you are in and move `simp at h` accordingly. (2) For list length contradictions: `simp [List.length_cons] at h` then `omega`. (3) `unfold f at h` or `delta f at h` to expand a definition simp cannot see through. (4) If `simp` makes no progress after `generalize`, the hypothesis still contains an unsimplified `if`-expression — use `split_ifs at h` BEFORE `generalize` to eliminate the guard first.

binder_annotation.error:
invalid binder annotation
T is not a class instance
binder_annotation.hint: Square brackets `[h : T]` are reserved for typeclass arguments only — Lean rejected this because `T` is not a typeclass. Change every `[h : T]` in the theorem signature to `(h : T)` (round brackets). Example: `[h : op = PLUS]` → `(h : op = PLUS)`.

hypothesis_missing.hint: `h2` is not in the local context — it was never introduced. Check the goal state for the names that actually exist there.

hypothesis_missing_split_ifs.hint: `h2` is not in the local context — it was never introduced. Check the goal state for the names that actually exist there. `split_ifs with h1 h2` names only as many hypotheses as there are if-conditions in that goal, and some branches have fewer.

guessed_lemma.hint: That identifier or constant does not exist in Mathlib. Do not guess lemma names. Instead prove the goal with `simp`, `omega`, `decide`, `rfl`, or by unfolding the definition and casing on the structure.

known_rename.hint: `Nat.eq_comm` does not exist. Use `eq_comm` (works for any type, no `Nat.` prefix needed).

app_mismatch_option.error:
application type mismatch
has type
  Option String
but is expected to have type
  Option Nat
app_mismatch_option.hint: You have `Option String` but `Option Nat` is needed. Extract the field from inside the Option with `.map`: e.g. `list.head?.map (·.id)` instead of `list.head?`.

app_mismatch_issome.hint: `Option.get` requires an explicit proof argument `h : o.isSome = true` — it is NOT the same as `Option.get!`. Use pattern matching instead: `rcases o with _ | v` or `match o with | some v => ... | none => ...`

app_mismatch_sort.hint: You passed a value where a proof is expected. The lemma takes a *proof* (e.g. `h : l ≠ []`) not the value itself (e.g. `l`). Pass the proof term, or derive it with `by simp`, `by omega`, or from a hypothesis.

app_mismatch_data.hint: A list lemma was applied to a struct's `.data` field, but the lemma operates on `List` directly — the struct's `++` is not the same as `List.append`. Fix: (1) Add `have happ : (s ++ t).data = s.data ++ t.data := rfl` (or `by simp`) and `rw [happ]` before applying the lemma, or (2) redesign the model to use `List T` directly instead of a struct with a `.data` field — this is almost always cleaner: just type-alias the aggregation as `List T`.

app_mismatch_arrow.error:
application type mismatch
has type
  A → B
but is expected to have type
  C
app_mismatch_arrow.hint:
`ih` is a function (type: `A → ...`) — you must apply it to a proof of `A` before passing it anywhere.
WRONG:  `le_trans ih ...`  ← ih is not yet a proof, it's still a function
RIGHT:  `le_trans (ih (by omega)) ...`  ← apply ih first
Common proofs for arithmetic preconditions:
  `by omega`                    — works for any linear arithmetic goal
  `Nat.le_add_right n k`        — proves `n ≤ n + k`
  `Nat.le_refl n`               — proves `n ≤ n`
If the induction is over a difference `k` obtained via `obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩`, also consider replacing the whole induction with `gcongr` — for monotonicity goals like `a ^ m ≤ a ^ n` with `ha : 1 ≤ a` and `hmn : m ≤ n` in context, `gcongr` closes the goal in one step without any induction.

app_mismatch_bare.hint: The argument has the wrong type. Common causes: (1) An induction hypothesis is still a function (has `→` in its type) — you must apply it to a proof of its precondition before using it as a value. (2) Passing a struct where a field value is needed — access it explicitly (e.g. `.id`). Read the expected type in the error and find or derive a proof of exactly that type.

type_mismatch_true.error:
type mismatch
expected to have type
  true = true
type_mismatch_true.hint: The goal has already been reduced to `true = true` (the field was unfolded to `true`), but you passed a hypothesis `h : x.field = true` where `true = true` is expected. Don't use `exact h` here — close the goal with `rfl` instead. If the goal still contains the field name, use `simp [h]` to rewrite it first.

type_mismatch_bool.hint: Bool equality goals like `x = true` and `¬(x = false)` are not automatically interchangeable. Use `decide`, `simp [Bool.eq_true_iff_ne_false]`, or `cases x <;> simp` to normalise.

type_mismatch_bare.hint: The types don't match. Check your annotations and coercions.

inhabited_generate.error:
failed to generate instance
  Inhabited MyType
inhabited_generate.hint: The type has no default value so `Inhabited` cannot be derived — do NOT add `deriving Inhabited`. Avoid `List.head!` and `l[0]!` entirely. Use `List.head?` (returns `Option`) or case on the list structure to extract the element safely.

synth_ofnat_fin.error:
failed to synthesize
OfNat
Fin n
synth_ofnat_fin.hint: You are indexing a list with a numeric literal used as `Fin n` where `n` is a variable — Lean cannot synthesize `OfNat (Fin n)` for a non-concrete bound. Case on the list structure instead of using `List.get`.

synth_inhabited.hint: `List.head!` and `l[0]!` require an `Inhabited` instance which the domain type may not have. Use `List.head?` (returns `Option`) or case on the list structure to extract the element safely.

synth_bare.hint: A typeclass instance is missing. Check your imports.

free_vars_bare.error: Expected type must not contain free variables
free_vars_bare.hint: `decide` cannot work when the goal contains free variables. Use `simp`, `omega`, `ring`, or `linarith` instead, or case-split on the free variables until the remaining goals are ground.

omega_string_length.error:
omega could not prove the goal
 a := "WEIGHTED".length
omega_string_length.hint:
`omega` cannot evaluate string literal lengths (e.g. `"WEIGHTED_SUM((".length`) — they appear as opaque variables to omega. String literal lengths are definitionally equal to their character count and can be reduced inline with `show ... from rfl`. Use this exact pattern:
  simp only [String.length_append,
    show "PREFIX".length = N from rfl,
    show "MID".length = M from rfl,
    show "SUFFIX".length = K from rfl]
  omega
Replace each literal and its count (N, M, K) with the actual strings and their character counts. Count carefully — every character including spaces and punctuation.
IMPORTANT: do NOT use `simp [String.length]` or `simp [String.length_append, String.length]` — `String.length` unfolds recursively and causes maximum recursion depth errors.
Also do NOT use `String.length_mk` — it does not exist in Mathlib.

omega_generic.error:
omega could not prove the goal
 b := (List.filter p t).length
omega_generic.hint:
`omega` reasons about linear integer arithmetic only — every other subterm is an opaque variable to it, which is why the counterexample it prints mentions terms you expected to have been reduced away.
Look at the `where` block in the error: if the same value appears under two different names (typically an unreduced projection such as `(a, b).2` alongside the `b` it should have become), omega cannot know they are equal. Reduce it before calling omega — `simp` the projection away, rewrite with the lemma that states the equality, or prove the arithmetic fact as a standalone `have` over the already-reduced form and close the goal with `simpa using` it.
Adding more hypotheses to omega will not help while the terms remain opaque.

already_declared.hint:
The generated code redeclares a name that Mathlib already defines (commonly `Path`, `Option`, `Prod`, `List`, `String`, `Nat`, or a tactic name). `import Mathlib` brings it into scope, so the definition collides.
Rename the local model with a prefix that cannot clash — `MyPath`, `SrcOption`, `ModelString` — and update every reference to it in the theorem and proof. Do NOT try to work around it with `namespace`, `open`, or `_root_.`: the theorem should model your function's own type, not shadow a Mathlib one.

uses_sorry.hint: Replace sorry with a real proof. Try omega, simp, decide, or rfl.

timeout.hint:
The proof timed out. Try a faster strategy:
(1) Replace `simp` chains with `omega` (Nat/Int arithmetic) or `linarith`/`ring` (Rat/Real).
(2) For commutativity/linearity over Rat: `ring` closes most goals directly.
(3) For a property about a specific enum/constructor value (e.g. `h : op = PLUS`): use `subst h` to replace the variable with the concrete value everywhere, then `simp [PLUS.getPrecedence, PLUS.print, ...]` to reduce the multi-branch if/match. Do NOT use `decide` or `aesop` on open inductive types — they do not terminate.
(4) For string injectivity (f a b = f a' b' → a = a' ∧ b = b'): use `String.mk.injEq` to reduce to `List Char` equality, then `simp [List.append_inj_iff]`.
(5) Avoid `aesop` and `decide` on non-finite or large types — they do not terminate.
(6) If the goal needs induction, make the induction hypothesis strong enough (generalize first).

function_expected_exists.hint: The term already has an existential type — you cannot apply it as a function. To extract the witnesses, use `obtain ⟨a, b, h⟩ := term` instead of `term arg`.

function_expected_mem_cons.error:
function expected
mem_cons_self applied to arguments
function_expected_mem_cons.hint:
`List.mem_cons_self` takes ZERO explicit arguments — all its parameters are implicit. Writing `List.mem_cons_self w` or `List.mem_cons_self _ _` is WRONG and will always fail. Correct forms:
  · To close a goal `a ∈ a :: l`:  `exact List.mem_cons_self`  (nothing after it)
  · To pass as proof to another lemma, e.g. `hweights _ proof`:  use `hweights _ (List.mem_cons_self)` — NO args after `mem_cons_self`, or use an anonymous proof: `hweights _ (by simp)`.

function_expected_field.hint: Lean parsed a space before `.field` as function application. Write field access without a space: `x.id` not `x .id`. Also avoid `head!` — use `List.head?` or case on the list instead.

function_expected_hastype.error:
function expected
has type
  a = b
function_expected_hastype.hint: `that lemma` is a theorem/proposition, not a function — you cannot apply it to arguments. Use `simp [that lemma]` or `rw [that lemma]` to rewrite with it instead of passing arguments directly.

function_expected_bare.hint: You applied too many arguments — the term is already a value or proposition, not a function. Remove the extra argument(s) and use `exact` to close the goal directly.

max_rec_depth.error: maximum recursion depth has been reached
max_rec_depth.hint:
Lean ran out of recursion budget rather than rejecting the proof. Raising `maxRecDepth` moves the failure and, pushed far enough, crashes instead of erroring — restructure instead.
The usual cause is `decide` on something that only looks small: a bounded `∀` over a list of `Char`, or a nested one over a table of pairs, evaluates a decision procedure across the whole type. Turn the membership into a disjunction and take the cases, so each branch is ground:
  simp only [theTable, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false]
  rintro p (rfl | rfl | rfl)
  all_goals rfl
For a long `if`-chain, `by_cases` with `rw [if_pos]`/`rw [if_neg]` costs far less than `split_ifs` or `fin_cases`.

heartbeats.error: maximum number of heartbeats has been reached
heartbeats.hint: Lean hit its heartbeat budget — a tactic is doing far more work than the goal warrants, usually a bare `simp` or `decide` over something large. Name the lemmas with `simp only [...]`, or case-split by hand so each goal is small. `set_option maxHeartbeats` raises the ceiling but rarely fixes the cause.

tactic_rfl.error:
Tactic `rfl` failed: The left-hand side
  a
is not definitionally
tactic_rfl.hint:
The `rfl` tactic ran and failed to close the goal. The two sides are not definitionally equal, so no amount of unfolding will close this. Prove it by `induction` or `simp` with the relevant lemmas, or check the statement is actually true — `rfl` failing on something you expected to be trivial usually means the model does not say what you meant.
The error prints the goal state after the failure — read it before rewriting the proof; it usually shows the goal is not the one you think you are proving.

tactic_decide.hint:
The `decide` tactic ran and failed to close the goal. The proposition is not closed, or deciding it exhausts the recursion budget. `decide` only works on ground decidable propositions; case-split the free variables first, and prefer explicit `rcases`/`by_cases` over `decide` on anything ranging over a large type such as `Char`.
The error prints the goal state after the failure — read it before rewriting the proof; it usually shows the goal is not the one you think you are proving.

unmatched.hint: Review Lean 4 syntax and ensure all imports are present.

unknown_identifier_unquoted.error: unknown identifier at the top level, no name in backticks
unknown_identifier_unquoted.hint: That identifier or constant does not exist in Mathlib. Do not guess lemma names. Instead prove the goal with `simp`, `omega`, `decide`, `rfl`, or by unfolding the definition and casing on the structure.
